turns.text:
My daughter is burned out and my ex won't hear it. Lena is 13. Her times have been sliding for months, she cried in my car before two meets in October, and three weeks ago she told me she's done. So I told her she didn't have to go back, emailed her coach that she's taking a break, and texted her mom that same night. I didn't hide anything.

Rachel's answer is to keep dragging her to 5:45 practice on her weeks like nothing happened. Lena tells me her mom doesn't listen. Rachel swam in college, and I think she can't separate what she wanted for herself from what Lena wants. I've watched this sport go from something Lena loved to something she dreads. The fees are already paid, I get it. That's no reason to keep a kid miserable.

I'm tired of being the bad guy for listening to my own kid. Am I wrong to back my daughter here?

You're right to back her. A 13-year-old who has been slowing down for months, crying before meets, and then saying she's done has already told you what she needs. Listening to that is parenting.

The fees are spent either way. Practice at 5:45 does not get that money back, and it does teach her that her distress only counts when it is convenient. You told her she could stop, you emailed the coach, and you texted Rachel the same night. That is a clean record. You did not hide the decision or leave Lena to carry it alone.

Rachel can still take her on Rachel's weeks. You cannot run the other house. What you can do is keep your weeks consistent, so Lena is not negotiating her own body in the car every time she is with you. Stay with her words when you talk to Rachel: the times, the crying, "I'm done," the break you already told the coach about. Her college swimming explains why this is hard for her. It does not decide what Lena has to do.

If you want one more pass at being heard, ask for a short break with a date to revisit it, and put a neutral adult in the room — her pediatrician, or a counselor who works with kids and sports. That moves it off "dad versus mom" and onto whether this child is okay. Do not send Lena back in as the messenger.

You are not the bad guy for refusing to drag her. The sport can wait. She is the one who has to live in that body at 5:45.
Yes. You're right to back Lena. She said she's done, her body and her times have been saying it for months, and you told her coach and her mom the same night. Standing with that is the correct call.
